Maladaptive Strategies.value: I try hard to control my emotions
I distract myself with something else
I throw myself into work or tasks to keep my mind occupied

Threat.value: Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen
I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
I constantly scan my surroundings for signs of danger

Memory.value: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together
When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop

issues.item: Self-Harm Distraction: I hurt myself physically to stop thinking about the event
issues.explanation: For a 64-year-old male politician whose trauma was as a relief worker in a war zone, this self-harm item is the only clearly incoherent element. The rest of the profile depicts classic war-related PTSD with sensory/social triggers, intrusive fragmented memories, and hypervigilant threat monitoring, plus avoidance/emotion-control strategies. In contrast, deliberate physical self-harm as a distraction is not supported by the surrounding pattern: there are no negative appraisal items suggesting self-punishment, shame, or self-directed hostility, and the formulation shows strong Triggers→Maladaptive Strategies links that are better matched by distraction and emotion-control than by self-injury. This item is not impossible, but within this profile it is the one element a clinician would most question as belonging to the same patient formulation.

vignette: Kamal had always been drawn to public service, and as a politician, he was no stranger to high-pressure situations. But it wasn't until his stint as a relief worker in a war zone that he experienced the kind of trauma that would leave an indelible mark on his life. The memories of that time still lingered, fragmented and disjointed, like shattered glass. It started with the smell of burnt rubber and smoke, a pungent aroma that transported him back to the ravaged streets of the war-torn city. He recalled the sound of gunfire, the screams of civilians, and the feeling of helplessness as he watched families flee their homes. The images were etched in his mind like scars, refusing to heal. After returning home, Kamal found it increasingly difficult to connect with others. Simple interactions with strangers left him on edge, his mind racing with worst-case scenarios. He would try to control his emotions, to rein in the fear that threatened to overwhelm him, but it was no use. The slightest mention of military topics sent him spiraling back into the darkness. To cope, Kamal threw himself into his work, pouring all his energy into his political campaigns and duties as a councilman. He became notorious for his long hours and attention to detail, earning the respect of his colleagues but also taking a toll on his personal relationships. His ex-wife had often complained about his absence, both physical and emotional, during their marriage. Despite his best efforts, Kamal couldn't shake off the feeling of being constantly on guard. He would scan his surroundings, searching for signs of danger, his eyes darting from one face to another in a crowded room. The unusual silence that sometimes fell over a meeting or gathering made him feel like something was off, like an unseen threat lurked just beneath the surface. As a result, Kamal developed a habit of repeatedly checking doors and windows, ensuring they were locked and secure. It was a ritual he performed with precision, a way to calm his racing thoughts and stave off the sense of impending doom that had become all too familiar. But the memories still haunted him, refusing to be silenced. When they resurfaced, Kamal felt like he was reliving the terror all over again. The emotions came flooding back, threatening to consume him whole. He would try to distract himself with work or other tasks, but it was no use - the memories lingered, a constant reminder of what he had witnessed. Lately, the strain had begun to show. Kamal's relationships with his colleagues and constituents were starting to fray, and his physical health was suffering as well. He knew he needed help, but the thought of confronting his demons head-on terrified him. What if he couldn't overcome them? What if they consumed him completely? It was this fear that finally brought Kamal to seek professional help. As he sat in the therapist's office, he felt a sense of trepidation wash over him. He wasn't sure what lay ahead, but he knew he couldn't keep living like this - trapped in a cycle of fear and avoidance, forever haunted by the memories of that war-torn city.
